P1: When the first seeder remains alive but hangs during filesystem work, `flock 9` blocks every other init container forever because the holder never exits and releases fd 9. The new comment incorrectly says this becomes an init crash-loop; retain a portable timeout/watchdog so a wedged seed is observable and recoverable.

<details>
<summary>Prompt for AI agents</summary>

```text

<comment>When the first seeder remains alive but hangs during filesystem work, `flock 9` blocks every other init container forever because the holder never exits and releases fd 9. The new comment incorrectly says this becomes an init crash-loop; retain a portable timeout/watchdog so a wedged seed is observable and recoverable.</comment>

<file context>
@@ -90,9 +90,11 @@ set -o pipefail
+# crash-loop either way.
 exec 9</nix-pvc
-flock -w 600 9 || { echo "Timed out waiting for the seed lock" >&2; exit 1; }
+flock 9
 if [ ! -f /nix-pvc/.seed-complete ]; then
   echo "Seeding /nix on PVC (one-time, may take a few minutes)..."
</file context>
```
